summary:
zyxilion explorer is a satellite-intelligence platform that detects active wildfires in near-real time and transforms 27 years of fire history (2000–2026) into predictive insight for the Dominican Republic's most vulnerable ecosystems the Cordillera Central, Sierra de Bahoruco, Valle de San Juan, and Los Haitises.

We ingest NASA FIRMS hotspots from VIIRS (375 m) and MODIS (1 km), capturing brightness temperature and Fire Radiative Power. Because the two sensors report different resolutions and detection counts, we built a harmonization pipeline: Uber H3 hexagonal indexing merges duplicate detections, and a Leave-One-Year-Out calibration aligns VIIRS to MODIS-equivalent counts (±2.4% error), correcting the artificial 2012 data jump so the historical record is trustworthy. An AI layer then ranks H3 cells by risk for the next 24, 48, and 72 hours, combining historical recurrence, live trade winds, and vapor pressure deficit.

This matters because fire response in the Caribbean is still largely reactive. By turning raw NASA satellite data into a calibrated, forward-looking risk map, Zyxilon helps authorities protect forests, biodiversity, and communities before fires spread shifting the paradigm from detection to anticipation.
details:
Zyxilon Explorer is an open-source satellite intelligence and predictive wildfire platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 (Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots). It resolves the historical 2012 sensor discrepancy between NASA MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m), eliminating an artificial +452% fire jump and providing a consistent 26-year calibrated wildfire climatology for the Dominican Republic and the Caribbean.

Operating on an automated pipeline, Zyxilon Explorer ingests Near-Real-Time (NRT) NASA FIRMS telemetry, removes industrial heat artifacts, discretizes the territory into Uber H3 hexagonal cells, and uses an ML model validated via Leave-One-Year-Out (LOYO) cross-validation to predict wildfire ignition and propagation risk at +24h, +48h, and +72h horizons.

The platform benefits forest rangers, emergency managers (COE), and environmental researchers by transforming reactive firefighting into predictive prevention, delivering critical tactical diagnostics in under 15 seconds. Its expected impact includes preserving critical biosphere reserves (e.g., Sierra de Bahoruco, Valle Nuevo), protecting national freshwater headwaters, and serving as a scalable framework for the wider Caribbean.

Developed using Python, FastAPI, GeoPandas, Scikit-Learn, Uber H3, Docker, Node.js (via pnpm), Tailwind CSS v4, HTML5 Canvas, and Leaflet, Zyxilon Explorer stands out through its creative aerospace-inspired cockpit, interactive 4D vector simulation canvas, and rigorous consideration of tropical island microclimates, trade wind dynamics, and low-bandwidth field usability
